chunks: Mūsā ibn Bakr narrated from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Aʿyan, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

“The people of two different religions do not inherit from one another. We inherit from them, but they do not inherit from us. Indeed, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has only increased us in honor through Islam.”

key_terms.أَهْلُ مِلَّتَيْنِ: people belonging to two different religious communities
key_terms.لَا يَتَوَارَثُ: do not inherit from one another

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith say about inheritance between Muslims and people of other religions?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal ruling concerning inheritance between people of different religious communities, affirming that mutual inheritance does not apply across two different religions. It also emphasizes that Islam brings honor and elevation to the Muslims, which is presented here as the basis for this distinction.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5723 - Musa ibn Bakr narrated from Abdur Rahman ibn Aʿyan from Abu Abdullah Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) who said:

"People of two different religions do not inherit from one another. We inherit from them, but they do not inherit from us.
Indeed, Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic, has only increased us in honor through Islam."
